title: Double X
html_source: In the 1770s, well before the birth of his world renowned Guinness Stout, Sir Arthur Guinness' focus was on the mass-production of Porter. There were two strengths of Porter at that time, either marked with a single or a double “X.” Soon to follow was a more robust third version, for export to the Caribbean. In 1820, the XX was renamed Guinness Extra Stout Porter, and soon after, the XXX gained the soubriquet Foreign Extra Stout (Guinness dropped the X Porter in 1974).
